newsitem.title: LEBANON: Syrian troop redeployment not worrying-envoy.
newsitem.headline: Syrian troop redeployment not worrying-envoy.

text.p: A U.S. envoy to Beirut described on Tuesday a Syrian troop redeployment in Lebanon as "not alarming", saying fears of a Syrian-Israeli military confrontation were "far-fetched".

"I think a lot of people in the region are watching closely the redeployment and trying to understand what the significance is and we are among those. I don't see anything particularly alarming in the redeployment," U.S. ambassador in Beirut Richard Jones said.

Asked by reporters at Lebanon's foreign ministry whether he expected a war in the region, Jones said: "I certainly don't see anything like that happening...(A military confrontation between Syria and Israel) seems pretty far-fetched".
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said earlier during the day that Syria's troop redeployment in Lebanon was an attempt to pressure Israel into making unilateral territorial concessions.
Syria has redeployed up to 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights, causing war jitters in Israel.
"We are taking seriously all the signs on the ground. I am convinced we are taking all the necessary measures to defend the security of the country and its citizens," Netanyahu said.

The redeployment began last month when troops left a number of positions in the central Lebanese mountains in what Lebanese security sources said was a defensive redeployment after apparent Israeli threats to attack Syrian forces in Lebanon.

"I think it is clear that you (in Lebanon) are in a tense situation but parties on both sides should assess the situation very carefully and should not rush to conclusions on what those on the other side may be planning to do," Jones added.
